name: USC-STAR
aliases: Studer pouch versus T-pouch randomized trial
question: Does the antireflux mechanism of the T-pouch preserve renal function better than the Studer pouch after orthotopic ileal neobladder reconstruction?

arms.label: T-pouch orthotopic ileal neobladder with an antireflux mechanism

design.population: Patients with clinically nonmetastatic bladder cancer scheduled for radical cystectomy with neobladder reconstruction.

verdictNote: No difference in 3-year eGFR change; T-pouch had more diversion-related secondary surgery.
takeaway: In patients with an ileal orthotopic neobladder after radical cystectomy (3-year renal data in 260 of 484 randomized), the antireflux T-pouch did not preserve renal function better than the Studer pouch (eGFR change −6.6 versus −6.4 mL/min/1.73 m²; p=0.35) and needed more diversion-related secondary surgery.

reports.label: Men's functional questionnaire
reports.citation: Ahmadi H, Skinner EC, Simma-Chiang V, et al. "Urinary Functional Outcome Following Radical Cystoprostatectomy and Ileal Neobladder Reconstruction in Male Patients." *J Urol.* 2013;189(5):1782-1788.
reports.followUp: mean 4.5 years (range 1 to 8) among questionnaire respondents

results.measure: Response rate to a mailed questionnaire sent to men at least 12 months after surgery
results.note: 68%; T-pouch and Studer participants are pooled and the abstract gives no results by arm.

results.measure: Respondents using at least 1 pad in the daytime
results.note: Among 179 male questionnaire respondents (T-pouch and Studer arms pooled), 84 (47%) used at least 1 daytime pad; among those 84 daytime pad users, 27 (32.2%) used mini/small pads and 19 (22.6%) used diapers.

Among 179 male questionnaire respondents (T-pouch and Studer arms pooled), 129 (72%) wore nighttime pads; among those 129 nighttime pad users, 19 (14.7%) used mini/small pads and 63 (48.9%) used diapers.
9.5% (arms pooled); 70.6% of them started within the first year after surgery.

reports.label: 3-year renal outcome
reports.citation: Skinner EC, Fairey AS, Groshen S, et al. "Randomized Trial of Studer Pouch versus T-Pouch Orthotopic Ileal Neobladder in Patients with Bladder Cancer." *J Urol.* 2015;194(2):433-439.

results.measure: Change in CKD-EPI eGFR from baseline to 3 years (mL/min/1.73 m²); mean difference, T-pouch minus Studer
results.note: eGFR decreased in both arms; the −0.2 difference is reported in Table 2. Three-year renal data were available for 260 of 484 randomized patients.

results.measure: Multivariable association of neobladder type with 3-year renal function
results.note: Baseline eGFR, age and urinary tract obstruction were independently associated with the 3-year decline in renal function.

harms.label: Urinary tract infection
harms.note: Cumulative risk did not differ between the groups; the abstract gives no incidence figures.

harms.label: Overall late complications
harms.note: Cumulative risk did not differ between the groups; the abstract gives no incidence figures.

harms.label: Diversion-related secondary surgical procedures
harms.note: T-pouch was associated with an increased risk; the abstract gives no incidence figures.

delivery.label: Enrollment period and allocation
delivery.value: February 2002 to November 2009: 237 patients randomized to T-pouch and 247 to Studer.

delivery.label: Setting and masking
delivery.value: Single center; treatment assignment was not masked.
